In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interferograms of the 1999 Athens earthquake are characterized by a complex pattern of deformation, which is mainly controlled by the local geology of the area.
the deformation pattern is a function of the time span of the interferograms, while the magnitude of the deformation is a function of both the time span and the baseline of the interferometric pair.
the deformation pattern of this seismic event is characterized by a combination of both extension and compression, which is in agreement with the results of the geodetic studies of the region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-seismic deformation pattern of the 1999 Athens earthquake is a combination of two main mechanisms: a pure strike slip mechanism and an oblique thrust mechanism.
the deformation pattern is highly dependent on the interferometric pairs chosen for the analysis.
the co-seismic deformation of Athens earthquake is a complex phenomenon and it is not easy to be captured by a single co-seismic interferogram.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deformation pattern of Athens 1999 earthquake is characterized by a combination of thrusting and strike-slip faulting with the thrusting component prevailing.
